summary.headline: Kanohar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 112% YoY to INR208.6 crore with 35% EBITDA margin; FY27 revenue guidance of about INR950 crore reiterated.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 112% YoY to INR208.6 crore, with EBITDA of INR73.1 crore (35% margin) and PAT of INR53.9 crore (25.8% margin). H1 FY27 revenue rose 109% to INR345.7 crore at a 32.3% EBITDA margin. Order book stood at INR2,711.2 crore at 30 September 2026, up 34% QoQ, with Q2 inflows of INR867.3 crore. Management kept full-year EBITDA margin guidance at roughly FY26 levels (about 28%) and reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of about INR950 crore, while declining to quantify FY28 growth beyond "similar" YoY growth.

financial_highlights.change: built up ahead of H2 execution

segments.name: Power transformers
segments.commentary: About 56% of H1 FY27 revenue, up 88% YoY; about 78% of order book. 400 kV is the largest product segment.

segments.name: Shunt reactors
segments.commentary: About 22% of H1 FY27 revenue versus negligible last year; about one-third of Q2 revenue; about 10% of order book. Mostly 245 kV with some 420 kV.

segments.name: Scott-connected transformers (railways)
segments.commentary: About 9% of H1 FY27 revenue (8.8% per Q&A); 220 kV and 132 kV only.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: 10.5% of Q2 revenue; EPC order book executable over the next 12 to 24 months.

segments.name: Voltage mix (Q2)
segments.commentary: 400 kV 46.6%, 220 kV 34%, 132 kV 7%, below 132 kV 1.9%. Products rated 220 kV and above were about 78% of H1 revenue versus about 53% in H1 FY26.

segments.name: End-user mix (Q2)
segments.commentary: Power transmission 57.1%, renewable energy 34%, railways 7%, power distribution 1.9%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR950 crore reiterated; management expects H2 to be stronger seasonally.
FY27 full-year EBITDA margin guided broadly in line with FY26 (about 28%), despite H1 at 32.3%; management cited quarter-to-quarter and order-to-order variation and full-year operating expenses.
Order book margin is at a gross-margin level broadly similar to FY26 and FY27 executed margins.
FY28 expected to show a similar YoY growth rate to FY27; specific number deferred to the Q4 FY27 call.
Gangol brownfield expansion on track for completion by the beginning of FY29; capacity expected to reach about 38,000 MVA by Q4 FY28 per management's confirmation of the analyst's figure.
Entry into 765 kV transformers and reactors targeted; management said it is 3 to 4 years before eligibility for regular tenders after first orders and track record.
capex_capacity: Current capacity cited as 19,200 MVA annualised; Q2 MVA sold about 2,130 MVA (including shunt reactors); management cited about 41% annualised utilisation in Q2 (the 10.5% figure used quarterly capacity).
Brownfield expansion at Gangol facility on track for completion by the beginning of FY29; management said current capacity suffices until FY28, with additional capacity needed in FY29.
Management said it would plan new capacity at around 80% utilisation of existing capacity.
Key bottleneck: high-voltage bushings lead times of 12 to 24 months depending on rating; CTC conductor supply not constrained. Production plans not affected by component constraints.
In-house manufacturing of tanks, radiators, control panels and insulation components; management said these cover most requirements.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of INR867.3 crore in Q2, including an order above INR250 crore from a central PSU; order book INR2,711.2 crore at 30 September 2026.
Management cited a 20% win-to-bid ratio (from the RHP) and a heavy inquiry pipeline without quantifying it.
Stable margin environment: management sees no pricing pressure from incumbent capacity additions, raw material increases or tendering.

Revenue per MVA about INR6.2 lakh in FY26; Q1 and Q2 FY27 higher (analyst calc. about INR0.8 million and INR0.98 million per MVA). Management said the metric moves with rating mix (shunt reactors) and raw material prices.
Shunt reactor market roughly 30,000 MVAR; typical ratings 50, 63, 80 and 125 MVAR.

Railways: about 1,000 traction substations over 5 to 10 years, roughly INR20,000 crore opportunity; timing depends on railway EPC tender awards. Company is one of two in 100 MVA 220 kV and one of four in 100 MVA 132 kV Scott transformers.
Company currently focused on domestic market, mostly government customers, with some private customers; exports not a current focus.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin (35%) well above the FY26 guidance and is the 400 kV vs 220 kV margin gap large?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premium 400 kV power transformers, shunt reactors and Scott transformers have broadly similar margin profiles; the order book carries a similar margin profile. A quantified 400 kV vs 220 kV margin gap was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 margin guidance (about 28%) below the H1 run rate of 32%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited quarter-to-quarter and order-to-order margin variation and full-year operating expenses; it said there was no one-off in H1 and no direct reason for guiding lower.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR950 crore revenue guidance conservative given H1 of INR345.7 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 is typically softer; FY26 H1 was about INR175 crore against a full year of INR650 crore, so the same split is not expected. INR950 crore guidance stands. A post-Q3 upgrade was left open.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capacity utilisation low and why expand capacity now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10.5% figure divided annualised capacity by one quarter's output; on an annualised basis Q2 utilisation was about 41%. It said ramp-up is gradual to protect quality, so new capacity is needed in FY29 and lead time is required.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter 765 kV and what are the steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Technology and plants are ready; the company is seeking first orders and a track record. It expects 3 to 4 years before eligibility for regular tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Does shunt reactor volume in Q2 count in MVA sold?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; MVA and MVAR are combined into one MVA figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: In-house tanks, radiators, control panels and insulation components; no plans for new components beyond these. In-house supply covers most needs.

risks_watch: Margin guidance (about 28%) implies H2 EBITDA margin near 24% versus H1 at 32.3%; watch H2 execution and cost trends.
Bushing lead times of 12 to 24 months and raw material (copper) price movement; price variation clauses were noted but inventory-based margin gains were rejected by management.
Capacity utilisation of about 41% annualised against planned FY29 expansion; execution ramp-up pace is uncertain.
New Scott transformer entrants could emerge; management said none known in the quarter.
Railway Scott transformer revenue timing depends on EPC tender awards and is not predictable by quarter.
Management declined to give FY28 guidance numbers and deferred to the Q4 FY27 call; watch for quantification.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line and order book, but cautious and evasive on margin: management repeatedly declined to quantify the 400 kV vs 220 kV margin gap or explain why the FY27 margin guidance sits well below the H1 run rate, citing variation between orders and quarters. Answers on FY28 and 765 kV timing were also deliberately non-specific.

adds.what: Gangol brownfield expansion (capacity to reach about 38,000 MVA by Q4 FY28)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR950 crore reiterated (H1 at INR345.7 crore, so H2 needs about INR604 crore), backed by a INR2,711.2 crore order book and Q2 inflows of INR867.3 crore; Gangol brownfield expansion is on track for early FY29, though the call gives no concrete capacity timing before then.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided about 28% versus H1 at 32.3%, implying H2 near 24%; management cited variation and full-year opex, not an expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gangol brownfield (98% size add, to about 38,000 MVA by Q4 FY28) is under construction and on track for completion by the beginning of FY29; no new capacity lands in the window before that.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H2 needs about INR604 crore to hit INR950 crore guidance after H1 INR345.7 crore, backed by INR2,711.2 crore order book and Q2 inflows of INR867.3 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 41% annualised, so a fresh capex is not needed now; management says new capacity is planned at around 80% utilisation, and Gangol is already committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said a post-Q3 upgrade was left open and H1 is typically softer; H1 is already 36% of the INR950 crore guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin guide implies H2 EBITDA near 24% vs H1 32.3%, and bushing lead times of 12 to 24 months and copper prices are cited risks; revenue guide reiterated.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 765 kV entry is targeted, but management said 3 to 4 years before eligibility for regular tenders after first orders, so no commercial launch in the window.

rows.label: Order book at INR2,711.2 crore
rows.why: Order book is up 34% QoQ with Q2 inflows of INR867.3 crore, and the EPC book is executable over 12 to 24 months.

rows.label: Railway Scott transformer opportunity
rows.why: About 1,000 traction substations worth roughly INR20,000 crore over 5 to 10 years, but timing depends on EPC tender awards and the company is one of two in 100 MVA 220 kV.

rows.label: Receivables unwind and inventory build
rows.why: Receivables fell to INR141.6 crore from INR210.8 crore QoQ while inventory built to INR196.8 crore ahead of H2 execution, so cash conversion should improve if H2 billing lands.
